questions.q: Which set should you look at repeatedly while comparing models and choosing settings?
questions.explain: The validation set exists for repeated experimentation. The test set must stay untouched until the final check.

questions.q: What does stratify=y do in train_test_split?
options: Keeps the class proportions of y the same in each split
questions.explain: Stratification preserves the class mix, which matters most when the target is imbalanced.

questions.q: You are predicting next month's demand from time-ordered history. Which split is most appropriate?
options: Train on the earlier period and test on the later period
A random shuffle across all dates
Test on the earliest rows and train on the latest
Use the same rows for train and test
questions.explain: Real predictions look forward in time, so the test set should come after the training data. Random mixing lets the model peek at the future.

questions.q: To get a 60/20/20 split with two calls to train_test_split, what test_size do you use on the second call, applied to the remaining 80%?
questions.explain: A quarter (0.25) of the remaining 80% is 20% of the total, leaving 60% for training.

questions.q: Why should you always set random_state in a split?
options: It makes the model more accurate
It makes the split reproducible, so score changes reflect real changes and not a different shuffle
It is required or scikit-learn raises an error
questions.explain: A fixed seed gives the same split every run, so you can attribute a change in score to your change, not to chance.
